extracted.intended_audience: corporate sustainability reporters, ESG/accounting professionals, and investors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for corporate sustainability reporting using SASB sector-specific KPIs and how those metrics should align with the CDSB Climate Change Reporting Framework (CCRF) and applicable financial consolidation/accounting rules. Includes specific guidance for consolidating GHG emissions data and aligning climate-related disclosures with TCFD recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sector-specific material sustainability KPIs (SASB)
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB developed sector-specific Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for sustainability that complement the CDSB Framework’s principles on reporting environmental information in the mainstream corporate report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These KPIs are intended to help public corporations disclose material, decision-useful information to investors. SASB provides a series of standards to reporting companies from all sectors; those sector-specific KPIs are used alongside CDSB principles to report material sustainability information.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG emission data consolidation approach (SASB Accounting Metric NR0101-01)
rubrics_metrics.description: GHG emission data shall be consolidated according to the approach with which the registrant consolidates its financial reporting data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach is generally aligned with Section 4.23 'Organizational boundary setting for GHG emissions reporting' of the CDSB Climate Change Reporting Framework (CCRF). Use the same consolidation boundaries applied in financial statements when consolidating GHG data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CDSB CCRF Section 4.23 for organizational boundary setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational boundary setting for GHG emissions reporting should follow the approach detailed in Section 4.23 of the CDSB Climate Change Reporting Framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer explicitly to CCRF Section 4.23 when determining which entities, joint ventures, associates, or interests should be included in GHG reporting boundaries to ensure consistency with the prescribed methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align GHG consolidation with IAS/IFRS consolidation and equity accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: The consolidation approach for GHG emission data is based on the requirements of the International Accounting Standards/International Financial Reporting Standards (IAS/IFRS) on consolidation and equity accounting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This means the approach should be consistent with how entities and interests (e.g., subsidiaries, joint ventures, associates) are treated in consolidated financial statements—i.e., include within-group entities or interests in joint ventures/associates in the reporting as per financial consolidation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference CDSB Framework for environmental information and natural capital reporting as further guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB standards reference the CDSB Framework for environmental information and natural capital reporting and use it as further guidance for certain environmental metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing environmental and natural capital metrics (where SASB standards indicate), reporters should consult the CDSB Framework for additional guidance on principles and methods to ensure consistency and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose material, decision-useful climate-related information following TCFD recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB and CDSB work together to facilitate the disclosure of material and decision-useful climate-related information in line with the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should align disclosures with TCFD guidance where relevant; SASB and CDSB provide complementary approaches and a joint paper outlining how their standards support TCFD-aligned disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards development through evidence-based research and broad stakeholder participation
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB’s standards and KPIs are developed through a rigorous process that includes evidence-based research and broad, balanced stakeholder participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users of the standards can expect that metrics are grounded in research and stakeholder input; this procedural quality contributes to the credibility and investor-usefulness of disclosed information.
